Description.Scope of Services: This project provides Skilled Labor for Waterway Cleanup Services throughout Santa Clara County to support Valley Water’s Unhoused Encampment Cleanup Program. The selected contractor will furnish all labor, equipment, tools, materials, and supervision needed to remove trash, debris, and hazardous materials from creeks, rivers, reservoirs, canals, and recharge facilities. Description.Scope of Services: Valley Water seeks General B contractors for the successful completion of the Water Quality Lab Counters project. The project replaces existing laminate laboratory countertops and sinks with new laboratory-grade epoxy resin work surfaces while preserving the base cabinetry. The contractor shall field-verify dimensions, prepare shop drawings for approval, and fabricate all epoxy components to the approved sizes, thicknesses, edges, cutouts, and openings. Provide all anchorage, fasteners, sealants, and penetrations necessary to achieve a watertight and chemically resistant installation compatible with laboratory use. Perform selective demolition with protection of adjacent casework and equipment, implement dust control, and maintain daily housekeeping so laboratory operations continue safely. Reconnection of water and waste services is an additive alternate to be performed by properly licensed plumbing personnel, with all joints sealed and leak-tested before turnover. Coordinate sequencing with Facilities and Laboratory staff, schedule any temporary service interruptions, and restore the space to full service at the end of each work shift. Deliverables include field measurements, submittals, product data and warranties, and closeout documentation with as-built dimensions and maintenance recommendations.

Description.Scope of Services: Valley Water seeks a qualified contractor to remove existing gates and furnish and install new high-speed roll-up doors at two Main Campus sites, Winfield Warehouse and the Crest Building in San Jose. At Winfield, the work includes demolishing two swing gates and installing a new door for an opening about 20 by 16 feet with a minimum opening speed of 60 inches per second, a multi-layer ultraviolet-protected reinforced steel slat curtain, new steel framing, a direct drive motor rated 1 to 2 horsepower, and a NEMA 4X control panel with interior push-button controls and no exterior access, with LiftMaster or equal acceptable. Valley Water will provide 460 volt three phase power within three feet of the control box, and the contractor will make all electrical connections to the control panel, floor loop, and photoelectric safety sensors. At the Crest Building, the work includes removing one existing roll-up gate and installing a new door for an opening about 20 by 7 feet with a minimum opening speed of 45 inches per second, a direct drive motor, NEMA 4X controls, an interior push-button station, and exterior integration by dry contact to an existing card reader.
